nodes.name: Webhook: agent-action
nodes.notes: rawBody: true is REQUIRED — the agent signs the exact bytes it sent. If n8n parsed the JSON and re-serialised it, key order and whitespace would change and every signature would fail. The raw bytes arrive as binary property 'data'.

nodes.name: Compute HMAC
nodes.notes:
The Crypto node, NOT require('crypto') in a Code node.

n8n's Code sandbox blocks Node built-ins unless NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_BUILTIN is set — which needs an n8n restart AND permanently loosens the sandbox for every Code node on the instance. This node does the same job with neither cost.

In n8n 2.x the secret comes from a CRYPTO CREDENTIAL (field: 'Hmac Secret'), not a node parameter. That is strictly better — credentials are encrypted at rest with N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY, whereas a node parameter would sit in plaintext in the workflow row.

nodes.name: DO THE WORK (replace me)
nodes.notes: Replace with the real downstream action — Jira, email, Sheets, whatever. `evidence` carries the citations that justified this action, so a filing can show WHY without calling back to the agent.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ accepted: true, executionId: $execution.id, run_id: $('Verify + dedupe').first().json.run_id, duplicate: $('Verify + dedupe').first().json.duplicate }) }}

nodes.name: Respond 202 Accepted
nodes.notes:
202, not 200 — the agent records this as 'accepted', never 'completed'. responseCode must sit inside `options`.

The body references 'Verify + dedupe' by name because the Set node on the first-delivery branch replaces $json.
